key_insight: Strong primary predictive scores did not guarantee well-calibrated risk estimates or consistent performance across patient populations.
clinical_relevance: Evaluating autonomous medical modeling requires calibration and robustness checks alongside primary predictive metrics.
method: Introduced Auto-MD-bench for survival analysis, classification and sequential prediction.
Evaluated AIDE, AI Scientist v2, Codex and Autoresearch against simple baseline models.
Assessed calibration and external performance across cohorts, hospitals and time periods.
evidence_signal: Across 15 tasks from 10 clinical datasets, the strongest agents achieved competitive primary scores but produced less-calibrated risk estimates than simple baselines.
watch_item: Benchmark results do not establish clinical safety; calibration and population-shift performance need validation before deployment.
paper_title: Auto-MD-bench: Evaluating Autoresearch Agents for Real-World Medical Tasks
